summaries.summary:
I reviewed UI/UX polish with Playwright at 1600x960, 1366x768 and 1024x640, the Electron minimum window size. Pages ran with a stubbed `window.desktop`, so the Windows title-bar padding applied, and with Vite's HMR socket blocked, because other engineers' edits were reloading the page mid-test. I screenshotted: the start screen, the gothic, crimson and noir templates open, every dock tab, every strip flyout, all 11 menus, the command palette and these dialogs (New, Export, Filter, Filter Gallery, Pose Studio, Remove Background, New from Template, Preferences, Shortcuts, About, Tips, Image/Canvas Size, Roblox Preview, Fetch Avatar, Place Asset, Fill). I also drove keyboard and pointer flows.

**What works:** the overall look matches ref5: dark, compact, Inter, violet accent used sparingly. Panels, Properties sections, the options bar (fits at 1366), toolbar tooltips and flyouts, the palette, Pose Studio, Export and Remove Background all look professional. The top-right 140px window-control area stays clear at every size, and every dialog fits at 1366x768.

**Main problems:**
1. **Blocker:** when the window is shorter than about 836px, clicking the Layer menu runs "New Layer" and closes the menu. This covers 1366x768 and 1920x1080 at 125% scaling maximized.
2. **Major:** dialogs don't take or trap focus. Tab goes to the Layers panel behind an open modal, and pressing Space there deleted a layer while the Export dialog stayed open.
3. **Major:** Libraries and Looks, the app's core features, are squeezed into slivers by the default dock layout on laptop screens.
4. **Major:** start-screen template cards are fake gradient placeholders with the name stamped on, even though real rendered previews already exist.

The rest are minor polish items.

Workflow review on port 5332 (server and driver now stopped). I ran the full path in a real browser: New 1920x1080 doc, then drag-dropped a Roblox Studio-style screenshot (sky plus baseplate), Remove Background, Character Styler, black fill, smoke, film scratches, dust and fold creases from Libraries, condensed, serif and kanji titles, Looks, a Vignette adjustment layer, and export. I also did a 1024 gothic icon from a green-screen render (grunge paper, torn border, swirl tendrils, blackletter title plus a faint offset copy via Ctrl+J, Ctrl+[ and nudge, then Gothic Poster style, clipped halftone, Long Shadow preset, Export with the Roblox Icon 512 preset). Then a 512 sunburst icon (sunburst rays, blackletter title with dashes, Sunburst Halftone look), and the Crimson and Noir templates (replace character, edit title, Styler on the placeholder). Save and reopen of the .pgfx project kept every layer, filter, effect and clip.

How close the results get:
- **Gothic (ref1):** about 70%. Paper, torn border, violet-rimmed tendrils, posterized character and blackletter title with ghost copy all work, but only after working around workflow-1.
- **Sunburst (ref2):** about 70%. The look's gradient map, halftone, glow and creases suit this style well, but its ray overlay also covers the character.
- **Crimson (ref4) built by hand:** about 60%. Layout and palette match. The smoke reads as puffy clouds, the character lacks ref4's red-tinted halftone, and a horizon artifact from Remove Background crosses the frame.
- **Templates:** the Crimson and Noir templates on their own look very close to ref4 and ref3. The weak point is getting your own character into them (workflow-3).

What works well: drag-drop placement, the Remove Background dialog (good once tuned), Styler param sliders, the type tool (Ctrl+Enter commits, ✓/✗ shown in the options bar), font coverage (blackletter, condensed, signature script, kanji), clipping masks, the vignette adjustment with its Properties panel, the export presets (512 output verified), undo history, and nudges merging into one undo step.

One thing I ruled out: a white export I saw at one point was caused by my own test setup (I had blocked Vite's live reload, so lazy-loaded modules came in as duplicate copies while other engineers were editing). After a clean reload the Export dialog rendered correctly, so it is not an app bug and is not reported.

Biggest problems for the user's goal:
- workflow-1: Remove Background's default mask output breaks the Character Styler.
- workflow-2: Remove Background's Auto defaults damage typical Studio screenshots.
- workflow-3: there is no way to swap your own character into a template.
- workflow-4 and workflow-5: Looks and Styler stack on top of what's already there and bury the subject.
- workflow-6: double-click to place assets doesn't work in the default layout.
- workflow-7: there is no way to save your own reusable styles.

I tested cross-module correctness by driving the real app (Vite on :5333 with my own scratchpad config that turns off HMR and file watching, so the other engineers' edits couldn't reload the page) through playwright-core: real pointer and keyboard events plus window.__app. I changed no project files and the server is stopped.

What held up:
- **.pgfx round trip is pixel-exact (max diff 0).** Tested on a document with every layer type: raster with rotate/scale transform, feathered mask at 0.8 density, two smart filters (one in multiply blend), five effects including two strokes and one disabled, and fill 0.8. Also a clipped overlay layer, warped gradient text with stroke, an angle-gradient star with dashed stroke, solid/gradient/pattern fills, nested groups (multiply and pass-through), procedural asset layers (one with an inverted mask), four adjustment layers, a hidden layer and guides. All 23 templates are also exact, and so is a Pose Studio rig layer: its generator params survive and "Update Layer" re-edit works on the reopened file.
- **Fonts on reopen:** opening the project in a fresh browser context matches the reference render within 500 ms, once fonts finish loading.
- **PSD round trip** is exact (max 1–3 levels) for every layer type except the adjustment layers it skips (see correctness-4).
- **Undo/redo:** undoing all and redoing all matched every intermediate state exactly (render hash, layer JSON and bitmap hashes). Covered a real brush stroke, a destructive blur, a smart halftone, a move-tool drag, a layer style edit, a text edit, applying the Noir look, Remove Background, a selection, crop and image size on the crimson template. Also rasterize, rasterize style, merge down, merge visible, flatten, rotate canvas and flip.
- **Closing documents:** with the clock pushed 120 s ahead so the 30 s grace had expired, closing another document never deleted a bitmap still referenced by the open document's undo history.
- **Switching documents mid-operation:** in-progress text is committed to its own document, and Enter in the other document doesn't touch it. A live Free Transform, however, is silently thrown away (correctness-6).
- **Sizes and zoom:** 64×64, 4096×4096 and even 16384×16384 documents work, including painting at 0.02× and 64× zoom.
- **Shortcuts:** I parsed all 315 commands (79 key combos) and 16 tool letters: no duplicate combos, no command shortcut lands on a tool letter, and no tool's own key handler swallows any command shortcut. Pressing b / Delete / Escape in all 77 visible text fields across the 14 panels never switched tools or deleted layers.
- **JS heap** stayed flat (41 → 44 MB) over 10 template open/close cycles.

What failed:
- Bitmaps are only garbage-collected when a document closes or history passes 80 steps, so pixel memory grows without bound (468 MB with nothing open; 768 MB orphaned after undo + new edit).
- Save and autosave read layer pixels after the document snapshot is taken, so a file can miss changes while the tab shows as saved (data loss in a timing window).
- A native dropdown keeps keyboard focus after you pick something: Ctrl+Z and tool keys stop working, and letters silently change the value.
- PSD export drops gradient map, black & white and vignette layers, which define the reference looks.
- Escape in number fields commits the typed value instead of cancelling.
- Free Transform is lost silently when you switch tabs.
- The PSD loses the document background colour.

Scratch scripts are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-perseverance/4ac78a5e-4d63-575b-a9b6-afba01734b7e/scratchpad/correctness/ (rt1.mjs, psd2.mjs, psd3.mjs, undo1.mjs, undo2.mjs, gc1.mjs, mem1.mjs, mem2.mjs, leak2.mjs, race1.mjs, race2.mjs, focus1.mjs, focus2.mjs, focus3.mjs, multi1.mjs, rig1.mjs, shortcuts.js, shadow.js).

I reviewed the app the way a Roblox GFX artist would meet it on first launch. I opened the start screen, menus, the template dialog, Help ▸ Tips, Shortcuts and About, and searched in the command palette. Then I followed the README's "Making a Roblox thumbnail in a minute" steps with a test avatar PNG: Crimson template → drop the render → Remove Background → Character Styler → double-click and edit the title → Safe Zones → Roblox Preview → Export As. I also checked each README feature bullet against the live registries: 86 fonts, 11 effects, 85 filters, 59 assets, 22 looks, 23 templates, 14 panels and 5 workspaces.

Most README claims hold, and the core flow works end to end. Remove Background, the Styler, safe zones, the preview and the export presets all behave as described.

**Most important finding (blocker): there is no working Windows installer.** Every "Build installers" GitHub Action run has failed. The Windows compiler rejects `src/filters/ui/FilterDialog.tsx` and `src/filters/ui/filterDialog.ts` because their names differ only in upper/lower case. As a result there are no Actions artifacts and no Release, even though the README tells people to download from those places. The only local installer, `release/Perseverance-Setup-0.1.0.exe`, was built on Oct 4 at 22:25, before the modules were finished, so it is out of date.

**Other main gaps:**
- **No way to swap in your own character.** Templates tell you to "replace the placeholder character", but nothing does it. Your image doesn't pick up the template's character styling, and the placeholder stays visible in the export.
- **Fake template tiles on the start screen.** They are coloured gradients, not real previews.
- **The guided tutorial resets.** Every action button closes it, and reopening starts again at step 1.
- **Key panels are cramped.** In the default layout the Looks and Libraries panels are tiny, and at 1366×768 the Looks panel shows no full tiles.
- **Minor issues:** two panel icons are identical, naming is inconsistent across menus and docs, Esc throws away text edits without warning, parts of the README are out of date, shared projects lose custom fonts without warning, and the Navigator's empty state has overlapping text.

**Testing notes:**
- I stayed read-only and changed no project files.
- Other engineers' edits kept reloading the default dev server and wiping my test state. So I ran Vite through its JS API with auto-reload and file watching off; the script is `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-perseverance/4ac78a5e-4d63-575b-a9b6-afba01734b7e/scratchpad/first-run/serve-noreload.mjs`.
- The server on port 5334 is stopped.
- The screenshots and test scripts are in `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-perseverance/4ac78a5e-4d63-575b-a9b6-afba01734b7e/scratchpad/first-run/`.
- An error about a missing `ALPHA_MASK` export in `src/filters/adjustments/math.ts` was a filter edit in progress, so I didn't report it.
- Not verified because the sandbox blocks outbound network: whether fetching an avatar by username works in the packaged app. The renderer calls `users.roblox.com` directly, there is no handling for that in the main process, and Roblox may reject requests from a `file://` page.

confirmed.issue: When the window is shorter than about 836px, clicking the Layer menu runs "New Layer" right away and the menu closes. The Layer menu is about 800px tall. It no longer fits below the menu bar, so it is moved up to top: 8px and covers the bar. Its first item, "New Layer", ends up under the cursor, and items run on pointerup, so the same click that opened the menu runs that item. Affected setups include 1366x768, 1600x800, 1024x640 (the Electron minimum), 1920x1080 at 125% scaling maximized, and any UI scale above 100%.
confirmed.evidence: Playwright, crimson template open, 1366x768 and again at 1600x800. Mouse down on "Layer": the .shell-menu rect is {top: 8, height: 756, scrollHeight: 800}, sitting over the menu bar. Mouse up: the layer count goes 23 -> 24, the menu disappears and the toast "New Layer completed." appears (screenshot menu-b-1366-Layer.png). Expected: the menu opens below the menu bar and scrolls, and nothing runs until the user picks an item.
confirmed.fix: In MenuLevel's useLayoutEffect (around lines 127-135), never move a top-level menu (level 0) above its anchor. Keep top = y and set maxHeight = innerHeight - top - 8; .shell-menu already scrolls with overflow-y. Apply the same height cap to submenus instead of shifting them upward. Also make onPointerUp (around line 158) ignore a release that is not preceded by a pointerdown or pointermove on that item, or that comes less than about 150ms after the menu opened.
confirmed.verifierNote: Reproduced at 1366x768 with the crimson template open, using a real mouse click on 'Layer'. Layer count went 23 -> 24, the menu closed and the toast 'New Layer completed.' appeared. At mouse down the menu rect was {top:8, h:756, scrollHeight:800}, and the element under the cursor was the 'New Layer' item. At 1600x960 the same click just opens the menu (count stays 23). Cause in code: MenuBar.tsx MenuLevel useLayoutEffect sets top = max(4, innerHeight - h - 4), and the items fire onActivate on pointerup. The proposed fix is sound.

confirmed.issue: Modal dialogs don't move focus into themselves, don't keep Tab inside, and don't restore focus when they close. Tab walks through the panels behind the backdrop, and Space activates whatever is focused there, so the document can be changed behind an open modal. A keyboard user also can't start typing in New Document (Name/Width) without clicking first. Enter and Esc do work.
confirmed.evidence: After Ctrl+N, document.activeElement is BODY. The first 10 Tab presses focus Layers panel controls behind the modal (layers-badge, fx, layers-disclosure, "Add layer mask", "Create a new group", "Create a new layer", "Delete layer") before reaching the dialog's close button. Export and the Filter dialog behave the same. With the Export dialog open, I tabbed to "Delete layer — or drop layers here" and pressed Space: the layer count went 23 -> 22 while the dialog stayed open (screenshot space-behind-modal.png).
confirmed.fix: In Dialog: on mount, save document.activeElement and focus the first [autofocus], then the first input, then the primary button inside .ui-dialog; fall back to the container with tabIndex=-1. Handle Tab and Shift+Tab in the existing capture keydown listener so focus wraps between the first and last focusable elements inside ref.current. Restore the saved focus on unmount. Add role="dialog", aria-modal="true" and aria-labelledby on the title. Make the New Document Name field autoFocus with its text selected. Optionally set `inert` on #root's shell while a dialog is open.
confirmed.verifierNote: Dialog.tsx has no focus management: no initial focus, no Tab trap, no focus restore, no role/aria-modal. After Ctrl+N, activeElement is BODY, and the first 10 Tabs focus Layers panel buttons before reaching the dialog's Close button. With Export As open, Tab went to 'Delete layer' within 10 presses, and Space dropped the layer count 23 -> 22 while the dialog stayed open.

confirmed.area: Dock layout on laptop screens (Libraries, Looks, Color, Navigator)
confirmed.issue: The default three-group dock gives the app's key panels too little height. Their fixed headers (tabs, a segmented toggle, the target line, search, and up to two rows of chips) use almost all of it. At 1366x768 the Looks thumbnails show as roughly 10px slivers and Libraries shows one row with its labels cut off. At 1600x960 Libraries still shows only one row with labels clipped, and Looks shows only the top ~55px of its cards. The Color panel has 715px of content in a 223px slot, so the sliders and hex field are out of view. The Navigator thumbnail shrinks to about 24px, and the Fit/100/150/200 pill covers its "No document open" text. The GFX Artist workspace has the same problem at 1366 (group heights 218/190/284px).
confirmed.evidence: Screenshots v2-dock-1366-looks.png, v2-dock-1366-nav.png, dock-1600-top-libraries.png, dock-1600-middle-looks.png, gfx-1366.png, start-1366.png (the Navigator pill sits over "No document open"), min-tpl.png at 1024x640 (Swatches shows one row, Layers three rows). DOM check: in the middle group, .fc-color has clientHeight 223 and scrollHeight 715.
confirmed.fix:
1. In Dock, give each group a minimum body height of about 170px. When the dock is too short to honour it, collapse the lowest-priority group (Navigator) to its header automatically, or let the dock scroll.
2. Compact the Looks and Libraries headers: put the chips in a single horizontally scrolling row, and merge the Active layer / Whole document toggle and the target line into one row.
3. Navigator: when the stage is under about 120px, hide the zoom pill or move it below the stage, and give the empty-state text room.
4. Consider making GFX Artist (Libraries/Looks first) the default workspace for this app, or picking it automatically when innerHeight is below about 900px.
confirmed.verifierNote: At 1366x768 the group heights are 178/198/316. With Looks active only about 10px of thumbnails shows under its header and chips. Libraries shows a partial row of cards with the chips clipped. In the Color panel .fc-color has clientHeight 168 and scrollHeight 715, so the sliders and hex field are out of view. The Navigator thumbnail is about 42x24px. On the start screen the Fit/100/150/200 pill sits over 'No document open'. The groups can be resized, but the default layout is cramped on common laptop screens.

confirmed.issue: The template cards on the start screen show CSS gradients with the template name stamped in big letters, not the real template. For example, Gothic Paper Poster shows a violet/grey gradient, while the actual template is off-white paper with a torn black border. Each name therefore appears twice. Real rendered previews already exist and are used by New from Template (useTemplatePreview). Square icon templates also get a taller art box (155px vs 113px), so card titles sit at different heights (y=641 vs y=598) and the grid looks ragged. The Quick Start card descriptions are cut off ("Experience icon (512 × …") and the cards have no tooltip. This is the first screen users see, and it looks unfinished.
confirmed.evidence: start-1600.png and start-1366.png compared with dlg-c-1600-template.png, where New from Template shows the real Birdcage, Sunburst, Exterminator and Eternity previews. DOM measurement: Gothic/Sunburst cards have art 155px and name at y=641; Noir/Crimson/Versus cards have art 113px and name at y=598. StartScreen.tsx TemplateCard renders .shell-tpl-frame with templateBackground() and .shell-tpl-glyph text and never calls useTemplatePreview.
confirmed.fix: In TemplateCard, call `useTemplatePreview(t.id, visible)`, with visible driven by an IntersectionObserver, and render an with object-fit: contain (letterboxed) inside a fixed 16:9 art box for every card. Keep the gradient only as the loading placeholder and remove the stamped glyph. Add title={q.description} to the quick cards, or let the description wrap to two lines.
confirmed.verifierNote: The start screen template cards render templateBackground() gradients with the name stamped on them (StartScreen.tsx:84-87), and useTemplatePreview (previews.ts:86) is never used there. The screenshot shows the square-template cards (Gothic, Sunburst) taller, with names at y=645 vs y=603 for the 16:9 cards. Quick Start descriptions are cut off ('Experience icon (512 ×…') and the quick cards have no title attribute. Template cards do have a title.

confirmed.issue: The Character and Fonts panels use the same CaseSensitive ("Aa") icon, so the strip shows two identical icons stacked a few rows apart. Only the hover tooltip tells them apart, which goes against the "simple and easy to understand UI" goal.
confirmed.evidence: In the strip, data-strip-panel="character" and data-strip-panel="fonts" both render svg.lucide-case-sensitive (screenshots hover-strip-character.png and hover-strip-fonts.png). Window menu rows show the same icon twice.
confirmed.fix: Give Fonts a different glyph, for example lucide `ALargeSmall` or `BookType`. Alternatively give Character `Type`/`Baseline` and leave Fonts as is. Check the name exists in lucide-react v1 before using it. Update panelMeta.ts:37 to match.
confirmed.verifierNote: Both tools/type/index.ts:50 (Character) and fonts/index.ts:21 register icon: CaseSensitive, and the strip shows two identical 'Aa' icons (y=165 and y=221 at 1366). The panelMeta fallback for character is already Type, but the registered icon overrides it. ALargeSmall, BookType and Baseline all exist in lucide-react 1.52.

confirmed.issue: The Type menu's text-only items stay enabled when the active layer isn't text, and running one only shows a toast. This is inconsistent with the Layer and Edit menus, which grey out items that don't apply.
confirmed.evidence: With the raster layer "Your Character (replace me)" active, enabled() returns true for type.fauxBold, fauxItalic, uppercase, warp, rasterize, convertToShape, toggleParagraph and editText (menu-a-1600-Type.png). Running type.fauxBold shows the toast "Select a text layer to turn Faux Bold on or off".
confirmed.fix: Make enabled() return true only when the selection contains a text layer or on-canvas text editing is active. Keep the toast as a fallback for shortcuts.
confirmed.verifierNote: In tools/type/commands.ts, toggleCommand, editText, warp, rasterize, convertToShape and toggleParagraph all use enabled: hasDoc. needTextLayer() falls back to the toast 'Select a text layer to …'. Confirmed from the code.

confirmed.issue: The first History row (the snapshot) cuts the document name down to one or a few characters ("C.", "Got…"). The secondary span .layers-hist-time holds the full label "New from “Crimson Film Thumbnail”" and is set to flex: none, so it takes the whole width. The class name suggests it was meant to show a time.
confirmed.evidence: Screenshots history-panel.png and dock-1600-bottom-history.png: the row reads "C.  New from “Crimson Film Thumbnail”". Relevant code: HistoryPanel.tsx lines 128-131 and panels.css .layers-hist-time { flex: none }.
confirmed.fix: Show only the document name in the row and put the label in the title tooltip, or show the time. Alternatively stack the name and label vertically in the 40px row and give .layers-hist-time `flex: 0 1 auto; min-width: 0; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis`.
confirmed.verifierNote: Reproduced. In the snapshot row, .layers-hist-label is 11.9px wide and shows 'C.', while .layers-hist-time is 172px wide and shows the full 'New from “Crimson Film Thumbnail”'. The cause is panels.css .layers-hist-time { flex: none } together with HistoryPanel.tsx:130-131.

confirmed.issue: Flyouts are a fixed 620px tall. At 1366x768 the Character, Brushes, Fonts and Roblox flyouts run past the status bar and cover Units/Pixels/Fit. Esc doesn't close an open flyout. Short panels (Effects with no effects, Roblox) leave about 300px of empty space below their content.
confirmed.evidence: Measured at 1366x768: flyout bottom is 760 while the status bar top is 744 (screenshot fly-roblox-1366b.png). After clicking the Effects strip button and pressing Escape, flyoutPanel is still 'effects'. Empty space is visible in flyout-1600-roblox.png and empty-fly-effects.png.
confirmed.fix: In Flyout's layout effect (around lines 409-420), measure the available height from the visible strip area above the status bar instead of the full side column, and keep top + h within it. Add a keydown listener: Escape calls setFlyout(null) when focus isn't in a text field. Use max-height in place of a fixed height, so the flyout can shrink to its content.
confirmed.verifierNote: At 1366x768 the Roblox flyout spans y=140 to 760, while the status bar top is 744 (right edge 1063), so the flyout covers Units/Pixels/Fit. Esc leaves flyoutPanel set (checked for both 'adjustments' and 'roblox'), and there is no Escape handler in Dock.tsx. The Roblox flyout has about 230px of empty space below its content. The cause is Flyout's layout effect, which uses the full .shell-side height and a fixed h of 620.

confirmed.issue: If a group has more tabs than fit in the 268px dock, the extra tabs render past the dock's right edge with no scroll or overflow menu. This happens after dragging panels into a group or using "Dock in Panel Group". The active tab can end up off-screen.
confirmed.evidence: With 6 tabs in the bottom group, .shell-group-tab elements end at x=1659 and x=1705 in a 1600px window. With Brushes active, its tab is not visible (docked-brushes.png).
confirmed.fix: Make the tab strip scroll horizontally, with scrollbars hidden and the wheel mapped to horizontal scroll, and call scrollIntoView on the active tab. Alternatively add a chevron menu that lists the hidden tabs.
confirmed.verifierNote: Partly inaccurate but the issue reproduces. The tabs do not render past the dock edge: .shell-group-tabs already has overflow-x: auto with the scrollbar hidden, so they are clipped. With 6 tabs, the active 'Character' tab sits at x≈1694 in a 1600px window and is invisible, 'Brus' is cut off, and there is no wheel handler, scrollIntoView or overflow menu in Dock.tsx. The fix only needs scrollIntoView on the active tab plus wheel-to-horizontal scrolling (or a chevron menu).

confirmed.issue: With no document open, the Adjustments panel shows two empty-state messages one after the other: "Open or create a document to add adjustments." under the icon grid, and then an icon with "No document open."

confirmed.verifierNote: Reproduced with no document open. The Adjustments flyout shows 'Open or create a document to add adjustments.' under the icon grid, then a collapsed 'Adjustment Presets' header, then a second icon with 'No document open.'

confirmed.area: Roblox ▸ Remove Background → Character Styler (core documented workflow)
confirmed.issue: With Remove Background's default output ("Layer mask", non-destructive), every Character Styler style is computed on the unmasked pixels, including the background. A green-screen render styled with Gothic Poster becomes a flat green silhouette. On a sky+baseplate screenshot, Crimson Rim's rim light lands on the hidden rectangle edges and the halftone draws the leftover horizon line. The Styler's safety check treats an enabled mask as already cut out, so it never warns.
confirmed.evidence: In a 1024 doc I dropped char-green.png, chose Remove Background ▸ Green screen ▸ Apply as Mask, then Styler ▸ Gothic Poster: the whole character turned flat green (screenshot g4.png). Undoing and redoing the cut with Output = "Delete pixels", then the same style, gave a correct posterized character with a violet rim (g5b.png). Code: src/render/engine.ts runs applyFilterStack at ~line 1417 and applyMask only at ~line 1425 (filters before mask). src/roblox/styler/StylerPanel.tsx hasOpaqueBackground() returns false whenever layer.mask is enabled. RemoveBgDialog.tsx sets lastOutput = 'mask' by default. README step 3 tells users to do exactly Remove Background → choose a style.
confirmed.fix: Feed the layer mask into the smart-filter input: when a layer has an enabled mask, multiply mask alpha into the content before applyFilterStack (at least for alpha-dependent filters: rim-light, top-shade, toon-roblox, silhouette, cel-shade outline, ink-outline, rough-edges, halftone with transparentPaper), or pass the mask in FilterContext. As a stopgap: (a) in StylerPanel apply, if the target has a Remove-BG mask, apply/bake it first or show "Character filters need a cut-out — Apply mask?"; (b) default RemoveBgDialog output to 'delete' when the layer has no filters.
confirmed.verifierNote: Reproduced. New Thumbnail, dropped char-green.png, Remove Background with Green screen and Apply as Mask (mask enabled), then applied gothic-poster (filters top-shade, toon-roblox, rim-light). confirmed.issue: The bitmap store is only garbage-collected when a document closes or history passes 80 steps (gcBitmaps), and anything created in the last 30 s is spared (retainOnly grace). So pixels from documents closed soon after opening, and from discarded redo branches, stay alive indefinitely. Nothing else ever triggers GC, so canvas memory grows until the Electron renderer runs out.
confirmed.evidence: mem1.mjs: opened and closed tpl-crimson-thumbnail 10 times (about 1 s each). Afterwards 0 sessions were open but the store held 64 bitmaps / 468 MB of canvas pixels; they were freed only after I faked +120 s and closed another document. mem2.mjs (10 different templates): 55 bitmaps left with every document closed. The render cache was correctly emptied (0 slots), so the store is the leak. leak2.mjs: 2048² document with 4 layers, three rounds of Image Size 4096 → undo → opacity change (which discards the redo branch). The store grew from 4 bitmaps / 64 MB to 16 / 832 MB, unchanged with the clock moved 10 minutes ahead (only 4 bitmaps still referenced).
confirmed.fix: In closeDocument, compute the bitmaps referenced by the closing session (docs + patches) minus those referenced by the remaining sessions, and delete them immediately with no grace. The tool's in-flight young bitmaps aren't in that set, so they stay safe. In commit, when entries after history.index are dropped, do the same for bitmaps referenced only by the dropped entries. Also schedule a deferred gcBitmaps (setTimeout of about grace + 1 s, debounced) after any close, trim or branch discard, so the grace window can't make bitmaps permanent.
confirmed.verifierNote: Reproduced (v_mem.mjs). After opening and closing tpl-crimson-thumbnail 5 times, 0 sessions were open but the store still held 40 bitmaps / 293 MB, and they were still there 3 s later. A discarded redo branch (Image Size 2048 on a 1024 doc, undo, then an opacity edit) left its bitmap in the store even with the clock moved 10 minutes ahead. In editor.ts, gcBitmaps is only called from closeDocument and from commit when history is trimmed, and bitmaps.ts retainOnly spares anything under 30 s old. 'Indefinitely' is overstated: closing any document after the grace period freed everything (0 / 0 MB), and once history passes 80 entries every commit runs GC. Still, hundreds of MB stay held until the next late close, and redo branches are never freed in sessions with fewer than 80 steps. The fix in editor.ts (free a session's bitmaps on close, free dropped branches on commit, deferred GC) is sound.

confirmed.issue: encodeProject takes the document JSON once but reads layer pixels one bitmap at a time across awaits (about 2.7 s for the noir template; autosave also yields with idle() between bitmaps). Pixels edited or undone during the save come from a different state than the JSON, yet saveDocument marks the history step it started on as saved. This is a data-loss window: Ctrl+S, then Ctrl+Z while encoding, then Ctrl+Y leaves the tab showing clean while the file lacks the change, so closing won't prompt. Autosave recovery files routinely mix states the same way.
confirmed.evidence: race1.mjs: committed a magenta fill on the last raster layer (state N), called encodeProject(N), then undo() on the next tick. The decoded file matched state N-1 exactly (diff 0) and differed from N on 64% of pixels (max 189). race2.mjs, end to end through saveDocument with the browser download captured: saveDocument() → undo() during encode → redo(). Result: saveOk = true, session.dirty = false after redo, and the saved file differs from the current document on 64.2% of pixels.
confirmed.fix: Snapshot everything synchronously before the first await. For each bitmap id, record bitmaps.version(id) and either reuse a pngCache hit (same canvas + version) or copy the canvas (drawImage into a new canvas) synchronously, then encode the copies. Or, as a cheaper guard, re-check after encoding that every id's version and the session's current history entry are unchanged; if not, re-encode or don't call markSavedAt. Apply the same snapshot in autosaveTick.
confirmed.verifierNote: Reproduced end to end (v_race.mjs, noir template, 13 bitmaps, edited bitmap is last in order). Ran saveDocument, undo 100 ms later, then redo. Save took 4.3 s and returned true. dirty was true after the undo and false after the redo, yet the saved file differs from the current document on 64% of pixels (max 189). In project.ts, encodeProject captures the doc JSON once but reads canvases after each await, and undo applies patches to those same canvases in place. save.ts then calls markSavedAt on the entry the save started from. Nothing blocks undo while a save runs (the 'saving' flag only blocks a second save). The snapshot-before-first-await fix is valid; autosave (encodeProject with background/idle) has the same exposure.

confirmed.issue: After picking a value in any native <select> (the shared Select control is used about 60 times: Layers blend/kind, options-bar selects such as brush Mode, ParamEditor selects in filter/effect/asset params, swatch set, status bar units), focus stays on the select. focusKind treats it as a text field (isTypingTarget returns true for SELECT), so every global shortcut is ignored, including Ctrl+Z and tool letters. Meanwhile the browser's type-to-search on the select changes the value on letter keys and commits a new history step.

confirmed.issue: toPsdAdjustment only maps brightness-contrast, levels, curves, exposure, vibrance, hue-saturation (without colorize), invert, posterize and threshold. confirmed.area: Multi-document: Free Transform on tab switch
